traits.inflorescence.note: Watson and Dallwitz's account of the family, as quoted in search results (the page itself was not read): flowers in umbels nearly always, or in heads. General accounts add that the umbel is usually compound, its rays ending in umbellets, as the family's old name, Umbelliferae, says; a simple umbel is less usual.

traits.note: Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, volume 3 (1951), read in full (Umbelliferae by Mathias and Constance): flowers small, epigynous; sepals usually 5, evident or often obsolete; petals 5 on the margin of the hypanthium, which is wholly adnate to the ovary (so no floral cup stands above it); stamens 5; ovary bicarpellate, 2-celled; outer flowers of an umbel sometimes radiant.
